notes_on_fields.vocabulary: All trait values are reproduced verbatim from the catalogue’s own controlled vocabularies. "Unknown" and "Not applicable" are catalogue values, not missing data.
notes_on_fields.reference_varieties: The catalogue is relative, not absolute. Arabica references: Caturra = Average bean size / Medium yield / Average ripening / Average outturn; SL28 = Large bean / Low yield / High outturn; Maragogipe = Very Large bean. Bourbon and K7 also = Medium yield. There is no Robusta reference variety for ripening.
notes_on_fields.optimal_altitude: The catalogue gives optimal altitude as a band (Low / Medium / High and combinations), not metres, because the metre equivalent depends on the farm’s latitude. "optimal_altitude" holds the catalogue band verbatim; "optimal_altitude_m" resolves it into metres using the catalogue’s own latitude table.
notes_on_fields.bean_size_scales: Arabica bean size uses Below Average / Average / Large / Very Large. Robusta bean size is given as screen size: Small (screen 14 or below) / Medium (screen 15-16) / Large (screen >17).
notes_on_fields.yield_scales: Arabica yield potential is categorical (Low / Medium / High / Very High). Robusta yield potential is given in kg/ha.
notes_on_fields.rust_resistance_caveat: WCR warns that because most rust-resistant introgressed varieties derive their resistance from a single shared parent (the Timor Hybrid), "most existing rust-resistant varieties will no longer be resistant in the near-to-medium term." Lempira (Honduras) and Costa Rica 95 (Costa Rica) are named as confirmed breakdowns.
notes_on_fields.non_uniform_varieties: T5175, T5296, Anacafe 14 and Pacamara are included despite not meeting the catalogue’s own definition of a variety — they are neither uniform nor stable from one generation to the next.
notes_on_fields.also_known_as_provenance: Alternative names come from the catalogue itself (Typica) and from the World History & Geography of Arabica Cultivars document. Varieties with no documented synonym omit the field rather than guess.
notes_on_fields.origin_provenance: Origin is the country or region where the variety was selected or developed, taken from the catalogue’s BREEDER field and the country lists in its front matter, or from COUNTRY OF RELEASE for Robusta. Omitted where the documents do not state it.

varieties.name: AB3
varieties.breeder: Indonesian Coffee and Cocoa Research Institute (ICCRI)
varieties.catalog_summary: High cup quality, adapted for agroforestry; limited cultivation in Java
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Susceptible to Pratylenchus nematodes. Well adapted for cultivation in agroforestry systems. Yield and rust resistance for this variety were globally evaluated at 23 sites in 15 countries as part of WCR’s International Multilocation Variety Trial. A variety's local performance may vary based on which races of rust are present in the environment.
varieties.notes: High cup quality, adapted for agroforestry; limited cultivation in Java. WCR rates high-altitude cup quality potential as good; bean size large; best at high elevation for its latitude.

varieties.name: Anacafe 14
varieties.catalog_summary: Very high yielding variety, with rust resistance and good quality at elevations above 1300 meters. Variety not uniform.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Anacafe 14 is drought tolerant. Anacafe 14 is not uniform; plants are not stable from one generation to the next.
varieties.notes: Very high yielding variety, with rust resistance and good quality at elevations above 1300 meters. Variety not uniform. WCR rates high-altitude cup quality potential as good; bean size very large; best at medium-to-high elevation for its latitude.

varieties.name: Batian
varieties.lineage: Composite variety containing parentage from: SL28, SL34, Rume Sudan, N39, K7, SL4 and the Timor Hybrid.
varieties.breeder: Coffee Research Foundation (now Kenya Agricultural and Livestock Research Organization, KALRO)
varieties.catalog_summary: A tall variety that combines high yields, tolerance to coffee leaf rust, resistance to coffee berry disease, and good cup quality.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Well-adapted for smallholders because of its rare combination of being a tall variety with disease resistance and resilience (e.g., can cope with low management and adverse environmental conditions). Yield and rust resistance for this variety were globally evaluated at 23 sites in 15 countries as part of WCR’s International Multilocation Variety Trial. A variety's local performance may vary based on which races of rust are present in the environment.
varieties.notes: Rare combination of tall stature, disease resistance and good cup — Kenya's answer to SL28's vulnerability, and a practical choice for smallholder Kenyan lots.

varieties.name: Bourbon
varieties.origin: Yemen, via Bourbon Island (La Réunion); to the Americas via Brazil, 1860
varieties.catalog_summary: One of the most culturally and genetically important C. arabica varieties in the world, known for excellent quality in the cup at the highest altitudes.
varieties.notes: The reference point for classic washed-coffee sweetness and balance: very good cup potential when grown high, but low yield and total rust susceptibility make it scarce. Average bean size, tall plant, early-ripening fruit.

varieties.name: Bourbon Mayaguez 139
varieties.catalog_summary: Vigorous and highly productive tall variety with very good cup quality. Found commonly in Rwanda and Burundi.
varieties.notes: Vigorous and highly productive tall variety with very good cup quality. Found commonly in Rwanda and Burundi. WCR rates high-altitude cup quality potential as very good; bean size large; best at high elevation for its latitude.

varieties.name: Casiopea
varieties.lineage: Caturra x Ethiopian wild accession "ET41" (CATIE collection)
varieties.catalog_summary: High yielding variety, with exceptional quality at elevations above 1300 meters.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: An important note about F1 hybrids: Seeds taken from hybrid plants will not have the same characteristics as the parent plants. This is called “segregation.” It means that the child plant will not look or behave the same as the parent, with potential losses of yield, disease resistance, quality, or other agronomic performance traits. varieties.name: Catigua MG2
varieties.catalog_summary: Recommended for specialty coffee production in Brazil. Broadly adaptable and drought-tolerant.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Wide capacity to adapt to different environments, tolerates moderate water deficits. It has shown itself to be less demanding in terms of nutrition and more tolerant to drought than traditional cultivars and others resistant to rust. Resistant to red mites. Cherries are strongly attached to the plant—a characteristic that helps reduce natural fruit drop but makes mechanical harvesting more difficult. Yield and rust resistance for this variety were globally evaluated at 23 sites in 15 countries as part of WCR’s International Multilocation Variety Trial. A variety's local performance may vary based on which races of rust are present in the environment.
varieties.notes: Recommended for specialty coffee production in Brazil. Broadly adaptable and drought-tolerant. WCR rates high-altitude cup quality potential as very good; bean size below average; best at high elevation for its latitude.

varieties.name: Catimor 129
varieties.lineage: Selection of a Catimor breeding line from Colombia (Caturra x Timor Hybrid 1343)
varieties.catalog_summary: High yielding/Dwarf/Compact variety resistant to coffee leaf rust and coffee berry disease. Found commonly in Malawi, Zambia, and Zimbabwe.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Requires careful management to maximize yield without overbearing.
varieties.notes: High yielding/Dwarf/Compact variety resistant to coffee leaf rust and coffee berry disease. Found commonly in Malawi, Zambia, and Zimbabwe. WCR rates high-altitude cup quality potential as good; bean size large; best at high elevation for its latitude.

varieties.name: Catisic
varieties.breeder: Instituto Salvadoreño de Investigaciones del Café (ISIC)
varieties.catalog_summary: Adapted to warmest zones and acidic soils. High yielding.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Susceptible to Ojo de Gallo. Adapted to warmest zones and acidic soils.
varieties.notes: Adapted to warmest zones and acidic soils. High yielding. WCR rates high-altitude cup quality potential as very low; bean size average; best at low-to-medium elevation for its latitude.

varieties.name: Catuai
varieties.catalog_summary: A compact plant with high yielding potential of standard quality in Central America. Very high susceptibility to coffee leaf rust.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Yield and rust resistance for this variety were globally evaluated at 23 sites in 15 countries as part of WCR’s International Multilocation Variety Trial. A variety's local performance may vary based on which races of rust are present in the environment.
varieties.notes: Brazil's workhorse dwarf, a Mundo Novo x Caturra cross. Average bean size and good high-altitude quality — reliable, unremarkable cup — planted densely at 5000-6000 trees/ha.

varieties.name: Caturra
varieties.lineage: Natural mutation of the Bourbon variety
varieties.catalog_summary: A compact plant with good yielding potential of standard quality in Central America. Very high susceptibility to coffee leaf rust.
varieties.notes: The catalogue's own yardstick: Caturra is defined as 'average' for bean size, ripening and outturn, and 'medium' for yield, so other varieties are described relative to it. Good rather than outstanding cup, and highly rust-susceptible.

varieties.name: Centroamericano
varieties.catalog_summary: Very high yielding with very good quality potential if planted in healthy soil and at elevations >1300 meters, with resistance to rust. Well-adapted for agroforestry.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: May have difficulty establishing roots in the first two years. Requires careful nutrition for roots to become established, avoiding too much nitrogen (N). An important note about F1 hybrids: Seeds taken from hybrid plants will not have the same characteristics as the parent plants. This is called “segregation.” It means that the child plant will not look or behave the same as the parent, with potential losses of yield, disease resistance, quality, or other agronomic performance traits. The variety should only be reproduced through clonal propagation and purchased from trusted nurseries.
varieties.notes: F1 hybrid (T5296 x Rume Sudan) with very high yield and very good cup above 1300 m. Must be propagated clonally — seed from these plants segregates.

varieties.name: Costa Rica 95
varieties.breeder: Instituto del Café de Costa Rica (ICAFE)
varieties.catalog_summary: High yielding variety adapted to warmest zones and acidic soils.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Recently, Costa Rica 95 has been confirmed through scientific evaluation to be susceptible to coffee leaf rust in Costa Rica and may also be susceptible in other areas of Central America. Susceptible to Ojo de Gallo. Recommended for acidic soils and soils rich in aluminum. Recommended for warmest zones.
varieties.notes: A Catimor whose rust resistance has been breaking down in Costa Rica — one of the varieties WCR cites when warning that Timor Hybrid-derived resistance is failing.

varieties.lineage: Naryelis (Catimor) x Ethiopian landrace accession "ET06" (CATIE collection)

varieties.additional_agronomic_information: May have difficulty establishing roots in the first two years due to an imbalance between root growth and aerial parts. varieties.name: Fronton
varieties.catalog_summary: Early production and high yielding plant resistant to coffee leaf rust. Well- adapted to low and medium altitudes. Found primarily in Puerto Rico.

varieties.origin: Ethiopia (landrace); selected and made famous in Panama
varieties.catalog_summary: Panamanian Geisha has exceptionally high quality at high altitudes. The term "Geisha" is often applied to other coffees that do not share the distinct genetics of Panamanian Geisha. Geisha is also cultivated widely in Malawi.

varieties.catalog_summary: High yielding plant adapted to medium altitudes. Resistant to coffee leaf rust and some nematodes.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Nematodes: Not resistant to Pratylenchus spp. It is resistant to Meloidogyne exigua.
varieties.notes: High yielding plant adapted to medium altitudes. Resistant to coffee leaf rust and some nematodes. WCR rates high-altitude cup quality potential as low; bean size average; best at low-to-medium elevation for its latitude.

varieties.catalog_summary: High yielding plant adapted to lowest altitudes. Requires high fertilization.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Recently, IHCAFE 90 has been confirmed through scientific evaluation to be susceptible to coffee leaf rust in Honduras and maybe possibly also be susceptible in other areas of Central America. Highly susceptible to Ojo de Gallo.
varieties.notes: High yielding plant adapted to lowest altitudes. Requires high fertilization. WCR rates high-altitude cup quality potential as very low; bean size average; best at low-to-medium elevation for its latitude.

varieties.name: IPR 103
varieties.catalog_summary: Good tolerance to heat, drought, and low-fertility soil. Adapted to various coffee-growing regions in Brazil, with high productivity especially in the early harvests.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: High rusticity, and highly resistant to coffee leaf rust. Very late ripening. This cultivar is more adapted to hot regions and poor soils. Yield and rust resistance for this variety were globally evaluated at 23 sites in 15 countries as part of WCR’s International Multilocation Variety Trial. A variety's local performance may vary based on which races of rust are present in the environment.

varieties.name: IPR 107
varieties.breeder: Instituto de Desenvolvimento Rural do Paraná (IDR-PR, formerly IAPAR)
varieties.catalog_summary: Highly resistant to coffee leaf rust, suitable for high altitude cultivation and mechanical harvesting.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Fruit ripens early relative to other varieties, making it a good choice for interplanting with other varieties to stagger harvest times and avoid the risk of later-season rains. Fruits detach from the plant easily, making this a good choice for machine-harvesting. Yield and rust resistance for this variety were globally evaluated at 23 sites in 15 countries as part of WCR’s International Multilocation Variety Trial. A variety's local performance may vary based on which races of rust are present in the environment.
varieties.notes: Highly resistant to coffee leaf rust, suitable for high altitude cultivation and mechanical harvesting. WCR rates high-altitude cup quality potential as very good; bean size large; best at medium-to-high elevation for its latitude.

varieties.name: Jackson 2/1257
varieties.lineage: A selection of Jackson. Bourbon-like genetic background.
varieties.catalog_summary: Very vigorous and highly productive. Found commonly in Rwanda and Burundi.
varieties.notes: Very vigorous and highly productive. Found commonly in Rwanda and Burundi. WCR rates high-altitude cup quality potential as good; bean size large; best at medium-to-high elevation for its latitude.

varieties.name: Java
varieties.origin: Ethiopia (landrace), selected and distributed via Java, Indonesia
varieties.catalog_summary: High quality in Central America. Tolerant to major diseases, with low fertilizer requirement. Good choice for smallholder farmers.
varieties.notes: An Ethiopian landrace routed through Indonesia, now valued in Central America for high cup quality at low fertiliser input. Large beans, tolerant of coffee berry disease, but rust-susceptible.

varieties.name: K7
varieties.lineage: Selected from French Mission. Bourbon-like genetic background.
varieties.breeder: Individual farmer selection: R.H. Walker in Kenya in 1936
varieties.catalog_summary: Tolerant to coffee berry disease. Found primarily in Kenya and Tanzania.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: K7 is distinguished by its spreading habit on young laterals, although older primaries tend to droop. It has characteristic medium to narrow leaves with young shoot-tips that are light bronze in color.Yield and rust resistance for this variety were globally evaluated at 23 sites in 15 countries as part of WCR’s International Multilocation Variety Trial. A variety's local performance may vary based on which races of rust are present in the environment.
varieties.notes: Bourbon-related Kenyan selection tolerant of coffee berry disease; the catalogue uses K7 alongside Caturra and Bourbon as its 'medium yield' reference. Good cup with light-bronze shoot tips.

varieties.catalog_summary: Tolerant of drought and coffee leaf rust but highly susceptible to coffee berry disease. Found mostly in Uganda.

varieties.name: Lempira
varieties.catalog_summary: High yielding variety adapted to warmest zones and acidic soils.

Recently, Lempira has been confirmed through scientific evaluation to be susceptible to coffee leaf rust in Honduras, and possibly also be susceptible in other areas of Central America. varieties.name: Limani
varieties.catalog_summary: An elusive Puerto Rican variety.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: "True" Limani is very difficult to find because of issues with genetic traceability dating to its original release in Puerto Rico. Consequently, plants identified as Limani rarely match the original reference. This doesn’t necessarily mean that plants identified as Limani won’t perform well, only that it is difficult to predict performance, for example, or resistance to coffee leaf rust. True Limani is supposed to be well adapted to medium altitudes (above 1000 m) and rust resistant.
varieties.notes: An elusive Puerto Rican variety. WCR rates high-altitude cup quality potential as good; bean size average; best at low-to-medium elevation for its latitude.

varieties.name: Maragogipe
varieties.catalog_summary: Good to very good cup quality in Central America, but highly susceptible to rust. Very low yielding, large leaves and large internodes.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Due to the low productivity of Maragogipe, Pacamara is considered a better option. Maragogipe beans are especially large, and the plant also has unusually large spacing between internodes and leaf size.
varieties.notes: The giant-bean Typica mutation: very large, low-density seed that needs a gentler charge and more time through the drying phase. Good to very good cup, but very low yield means it is rarely offered.

varieties.notes: Sarchimor with rust resistance and, unusually for an introgressed variety, notably high acidity in the cup. Adapted to medium altitudes, so expect a softer acidity ceiling than high-grown Bourbons.

varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Nematodes: Variety not resistant to Pratylenchus spp. Is resistant to some Meloidogyne spp. An important note about F1 hybrids: Seeds taken from hybrid plants will not have the same characteristics as the parent plants. This is called “segregation.” It means that the child plant will not look or behave the same as the parent, with potential losses of yield, disease resistance, quality, or other agronomic performance traits. The variety should only be reproduced through clonal propagation and purchased from trusted nurseries.
varieties.notes: Very high yielding variety if planted in healthy soil, with very good quality at elevations above 1300 meters. Well-adapted to agroforestery conditions. WCR rates high-altitude cup quality potential as very good; bean size large; best at medium-to-high elevation for its latitude.

varieties.name: Mundo Novo
varieties.catalog_summary: A vigorous and productive plant with good quality cup but susceptible to major diseases. Grown widely in South America, but rarely in Central America and the Caribbean.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Yield and rust resistance for this variety were globally evaluated at 23 sites in 15 countries as part of WCR’s International Multilocation Variety Trial. A variety's local performance may vary based on which races of rust are present in the environment. Very high vegetative vigor, excellent response to pruning, and suitable for mechanical harvesting. In Peru, the recommended elevation is >1500m.
varieties.notes: Vigorous tall Typica x Bourbon hybrid behind much of Brazil's supply. Good cup at altitude, average beans, and it responds well to pruning and mechanical harvest, but it is fully rust-susceptible.

varieties.name: Nayarita
varieties.lineage: Naryelis (Catimor) x wild Ethiopian accession "ET26" (CATIE collection)
varieties.catalog_summary: High yielding variety at high altitudes with very good cup quality.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: An important note about F1 hybrids: Seeds taken from hybrid plants will not have the same characteristics as the parent plants. This is called “segregation.” It means that the child plant will not look or behave the same as the parent, with potential losses of yield, disease resistance, quality, or other agronomic performance traits. The variety should only be reproduced through clonal propagation and purchased from trusted nurseries.
varieties.notes: High yielding variety at high altitudes with very good cup quality. WCR rates high-altitude cup quality potential as very good; bean size large; best at high elevation for its latitude.

varieties.name: Nemaya (Coffea canephora)
varieties.lineage: C. canephora T3561 x C. canephora T3751
varieties.catalog_summary: A Robusta variety used for rootstock grafting because of its high resistance to nematodes. Arabica plants (any variety) can be grafted onto Nemaya roostock to make the plant resistant to nematodes.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Grafting Arabica onto Robusta rootstock has no effect on cup quality. Propagation by seeds produced in authorized fields. Nematodes: Tolerant to Pratylenchus spp. and resistant to Meloidogyne exigua, M. arenaria, and M. paranaensis.
varieties.notes: A Robusta variety used for rootstock grafting because of its high resistance to nematodes. Arabica plants (any variety) can be grafted onto Nemaya roostock to make the plant resistant to nematodes.

varieties.name: Nyasaland
varieties.origin: Malawi (formerly Nyasaland), from Jamaican Typica; grown in Uganda
varieties.catalog_summary: Good cup quality, but susceptible to major diseases. Preferred by smallholder farmers in Uganda.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Resilient variety (e.g., can cope with low management and adverse environmental conditions).
varieties.notes: Good cup quality, but susceptible to major diseases. Preferred by smallholder farmers in Uganda. WCR rates high-altitude cup quality potential as good; bean size average; best at medium-to-high elevation for its latitude.

varieties.name: Obata (Red)
varieties.lineage: Timor Hybrid 832/2 x Villa Sarchi CIFC 971/10
varieties.catalog_summary: A high yielding, rust-resistant Brazilian variety recently introduced to Costa Rica.
varieties.notes: Brazil's widely planted Sarchimor: rust-resistant, high-yielding, adapted to medium altitudes. Cup is good rather than exceptional.

varieties.name: Oro Azteca
varieties.breeder: Instituto Nacional de Investigaciones Forestales, Agrícolas y Pecuarias (INIFAP), Mexico
varieties.catalog_summary: Adapted to warmest zones and acidic soils. High yielding.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Yield and rust resistance for this variety were globally evaluated at 23 sites in 15 countries as part of WCR’s International Multilocation Variety Trial. A variety's local performance may vary based on which races of rust are present in the environment. Susceptible to Ojo de Gallo. Recommended for acidic soils, soils rich in aluminium, and for warmest zones.
varieties.notes: Adapted to warmest zones and acidic soils. High yielding. WCR rates high-altitude cup quality potential as good; bean size average; best at low-to-medium elevation for its latitude.

varieties.name: Pacamara
varieties.breeder: Instituto Salvadoreño de Investigaciones del Café (ISIC)
varieties.catalog_summary: Capable of producing exceptional cup quality. Very high susceptibility to coffee leaf rust. Variety not uniform; plants are not stable from one generation to the next.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Highly susceptible to the Ojo de Gallo disease. Pacamara is not homogeneous; plants are not stable from one generation to the next.Yield and rust resistance for this variety were globally evaluated at 23 sites in 15 countries as part of WCR’s International Multilocation Variety Trial. A variety's local performance may vary based on which races of rust are present in the environment.
varieties.notes: Pacas x Maragogipe, with very large beans that roast unevenly against normal screens — expect to slow the drying phase and watch for scorching. Exceptional high-altitude cup potential but low yield and not genetically stable.

varieties.name: Pacas
varieties.breeder: Instituto Salvadoreño de Investigaciones del Café (ISIC)
varieties.catalog_summary: Standard quality in Central America. Very high susceptibility to coffee leaf rust.
varieties.notes: El Salvador's dwarf Bourbon mutation — standard Central American cup quality, average beans, planted densely. Very high rust susceptibility.

varieties.name: Pache
varieties.catalog_summary: A compact plant with medium yield and good quality, but highly susceptible to major diseases.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: It is best adapted to elevations above 1200 meters and in regions with less than 2,500 millimeters of rainfall per year areas. Recommended elevation in Peru is >1400 meters.
varieties.notes: Compact Typica mutation, medium yield and good cup, best above 1200 m and in drier regions. Highly susceptible to the major diseases.

varieties.name: Parainema
varieties.catalog_summary: Well-adapted to medium altitudes, resistant to coffee leaf rust and some nematodes.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Yield and rust resistance for this variety were globally evaluated at 23 sites in 15 countries as part of WCR’s International Multilocation Variety Trial. A variety's local performance may vary based on which races of rust are present in the environment. Nematodes: Not resistant to Pratylenchus spp. Is resistant to some Meloidogyne spp.
varieties.notes: Honduran Sarchimor selection (from T5296) that cups well for an introgressed variety and carries nematode resistance — a common specialty-grade rust-resistant option.

varieties.name: Paraiso
varieties.breeder: EPAMIG and the Federal University of Viçosa (UFV)
varieties.catalog_summary: Very high-yielding and rust-resistant compact variety developed in Brazil and recently introduced to Central America.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: High vegetative vigor, excellent response to pruning and ease of mechanized harvesting. It produces less in the first harvests, increasing productivity over the years. Excellent response to pruning. Widly cultivated in Minas Gerais, Brazil. Yield and rust resistance for this variety were globally evaluated at 23 sites in 15 countries as part of WCR’s International Multilocation Variety Trial. A variety's local performance may vary based on which races of rust are present in the environment.
varieties.notes: Very high-yielding and rust-resistant compact variety developed in Brazil and recently introduced to Central America. WCR rates high-altitude cup quality potential as good; bean size large; best at medium elevation for its latitude.

varieties.name: Pop3303/21
varieties.lineage: A selection of BMJ (Blue Mountain Jamaica) in Rwanda, related to but distinct from Typica.
varieties.catalog_summary: High yielding with tolerance to drought, coffee leaf rust, and coffee berry disease. Adapted to a wide range of ecosystems. Found mostly in Rwanda.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Drought tolerant. Significantly prone to die back.
varieties.notes: High yielding with tolerance to drought, coffee leaf rust, and coffee berry disease. Adapted to a wide range of ecosystems. Found mostly in Rwanda. WCR rates high-altitude cup quality potential as good; bean size average; best at medium-to-high elevation for its latitude.

varieties.name: RAB C15
varieties.lineage: A selection of the Indian variety Sln.6 (Kent x C. robusta). A population composite variety.
varieties.catalog_summary: High yielding tall variety resistant to rust and coffee berry disease recently released in Rwanda.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Vigorous.
varieties.notes: High yielding tall variety resistant to rust and coffee berry disease recently released in Rwanda. WCR rates high-altitude cup quality potential as very good; bean size large; best at medium-to-high elevation for its latitude.

varieties.name: Ruiru 11
varieties.lineage: Composite variety made of many varieties. Catimor (female parent) x multicross selection involving K7, SL28, N39, Rume Sudan, among others (male parent).
varieties.breeder: Coffee Research Foundation (now Kenya Agricultural and Livestock Research Organization, KALRO)
varieties.catalog_summary: High-yielding, Dwarf/Compact hybrid tolerant to coffee leaf rust and resistant to coffee berry disease (CBD). Released in Kenya.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Yield and rust resistance for this variety were globally evaluated at 23 sites in 15 countries as part of WCR’s International Multilocation Variety Trial. A variety's local performance may vary based on which races of rust are present in the environment.
varieties.notes: Kenyan compact composite bred for rust tolerance and coffee berry disease resistance. High yield, but historically cups below SL28/SL34 from the same farms.

varieties.name: S4808
varieties.catalog_summary: An Indian breeding line this is not yet commercially released.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Yield and rust resistance for this variety were globally evaluated at 23 sites in 15 countries as part of WCR’s International Multilocation Variety Trial. A variety's local performance may vary based on which races of rust are present in the environment. This variety demonstrates high rust resistance in global trials, but is considered susceptible in India where it was developed and is predominantly grown. India has the world's largest concentration of coffee leaf rust races.
varieties.notes: An Indian breeding line this is not yet commercially released. WCR rates high-altitude cup quality potential as good; bean size large; best at low-to-medium elevation for its latitude.

varieties.name: S795
varieties.catalog_summary: High-yielding variety that is widely cultivated in India.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Yield and rust resistance for this variety were globally evaluated at 23 sites in 15 countries as part of WCR’s International Multilocation Variety Trial. A variety's local performance may vary based on which races of rust are present in the environment. This variety demonstrates high rust resistance in global trials, but is considered susceptible in India where it was developed and is predominantly grown. India has the world's largest concentration of coffee leaf rust races.
varieties.notes: High-yielding variety that is widely cultivated in India. WCR rates high-altitude cup quality potential as very good; bean size large; best at medium-to-high elevation for its latitude.

varieties.name: SL14
varieties.catalog_summary: A good-yielding tall variety with drought and cold tolerance. Found mostly in Kenya and Uganda.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Drought and cold tolerant.
varieties.notes: The drought- and cold-tolerant SL selection, mostly Ugandan and Kenyan. Good rather than exceptional cup, but dependable in marginal conditions.

varieties.name: SL28
varieties.lineage: Selection of "Tanganika Drought Resistant." Bourbon-like genetic background.
varieties.catalog_summary: Drought tolerant and very good cup quality potential, but susceptible to major diseases. Found commonly in Kenya, Malawi, Uganda, Zimbabwe.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Yield and rust resistance for this variety were globally evaluated at 23 sites in 15 countries as part of WCR’s International Multilocation Variety Trial. A variety's local performance may vary based on which races of rust are present in the environment. Drought tolerant. Shoot tips are mainly green but occasionally bronze types are observed. Primary branches are predominantly semi-erect, but tend to become decumbent or drooping after successive crop-bearing seasons.
varieties.notes: Africa's quality benchmark and the catalogue's reference for 'large' bean size and 'low' yield. Exceptional high-altitude cup — the blackcurrant Kenyan profile — with high cherry-to-green outturn but full disease susceptibility.

varieties.name: SL34
varieties.catalog_summary: Exceptional cup quality but highly susceptible to coffee berry disease. Found mostly in Kenya.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: SL34 is adapted to high altitude areas with good rainfall. It is characterized by dark bronze shoot tipped plants with a few green-tipped strains. The laterals have semi-erect habit which tend to droop on older primary branches.
varieties.notes: Exceptional high-altitude cup quality, often blended with SL28 in Kenyan lots. Large beans, drought-adapted to high-rainfall highlands, but highly susceptible to coffee berry disease.

varieties.name: Sln.5B
varieties.catalog_summary: High yield and strong rust tolerance coming from both robusta and liberica parentage.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Yield and rust resistance for this variety were globally evaluated at 23 sites in 15 countries as part of WCR’s International Multilocation Variety Trial. A variety's local performance may vary based on which races of rust are present in the environment. This variety demonstrates high rust resistance in global trials, but is considered susceptible in India where it was developed and is predominantly grown. India has the world's largest concentration of coffee leaf rust races.
varieties.notes: High yield and strong rust tolerance coming from both robusta and liberica parentage. WCR rates high-altitude cup quality potential as good; bean size large; best at high elevation for its latitude.

varieties.name: Sln.6
varieties.lineage: C. canephora cv. S.274 x C. arabica cv. "Kent"
varieties.catalog_summary: Adapted to mid-to-high altitude Indian tropics, with good rust resistance and yields.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Well adapted for cultivation in agroforestry systems. Yield and rust resistance for this variety were globally evaluated at 23 sites in 15 countries as part of WCR’s International Multilocation Variety Trial. A variety's local performance may vary based on which races of rust are present in the environment. This variety demonstrates high rust resistance in global trials, but is considered susceptible in India where it was developed and is predominantly grown. India has the world's largest concentration of coffee leaf rust races.
varieties.notes: Adapted to mid-to-high altitude Indian tropics, with good rust resistance and yields. WCR rates high-altitude cup quality potential as good; bean size large; best at medium elevation for its latitude.

varieties.name: Starmaya
varieties.lineage: Marsallesa x wild Ethiopian/Sudanese natural mutant
varieties.catalog_summary: High yielding plant adapted to medium altitudes. Notably high acidity in the cup.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Variety not uniform. When planted, approximately 15% of plants will "segregate" (have different appearance/performance than the standard).An important note about F1 hybrids: Seeds taken from hybrid plants will not have the same characteristics as the parent plants. This is called “segregation.” It means that the child plant will not look or behave the same as the parent, with potential losses of yield, disease resistance, quality, or other agronomic performance traits. The variety should only be reproduced through clonal propagation and purchased from trusted nurseries.
varieties.notes: The first F1 hybrid propagated by seed rather than clonally. High yield at medium altitudes with notably high acidity, though roughly 15% of plants segregate.

varieties.name: T5175
varieties.breeder: Instituto del Café de Costa Rica (ICAFE)
varieties.catalog_summary: High-yielding plant adapted to lowest altitudes. Requires high fertilization. Variety not uniform.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Highly susceptible to Ojo de Gallo. T5175 is not homogeneous; plants are not stable from one generation to the next.
varieties.notes: High-yielding plant adapted to lowest altitudes. Requires high fertilization. Variety not uniform. WCR rates high-altitude cup quality potential as very low; bean size average; best at low-to-medium elevation for its latitude.

varieties.name: T5296
varieties.lineage: Timor Hybrid CIFC 832/2 x Villa Sarchi
varieties.catalog_summary: Well-adapted to medium altitudes. Variety not uniform.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: T5296 not uniform; plants are not stable from one generation to the next. Nematodes: Not resistant to Pratylenchus spp. There may be varying degrees of resistance to Meloidogyne exigua.
varieties.notes: Well-adapted to medium altitudes. Variety not uniform. WCR rates high-altitude cup quality potential as good; bean size large; best at low-to-medium elevation for its latitude.

varieties.name: T8667
varieties.catalog_summary: High-yielding variety, resistant to rust, and adapted to warmest zones and acidic soils.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Susceptible to Ojo de Gallo, recommended for acidic soils and soils rich in aluminum, as well as warm climates. In Peru, the recommended elevation is between 800 and 1400 meters.
varieties.notes: High-yielding variety, resistant to rust, and adapted to warmest zones and acidic soils. WCR rates high-altitude cup quality potential as low; bean size average; best at low-to-medium elevation for its latitude.

varieties.name: Tekisic
varieties.lineage: A selection of the Bourbon variety
varieties.breeder: Instituto Salvadoreño de Investigaciones del Café (ISIC)
varieties.catalog_summary: A variety selected in El Salvador, and known for very good cup quality in the highest altitudes.
varieties.notes: A Salvadoran mass-selection of Bourbon prized for very good cup at the highest altitudes; effectively an improved Bourbon with the same rust vulnerability.

varieties.name: Typica
varieties.lineage: Also called Criollo (Creole), Indio (Indian), Arábigo (Arabica), Plume Hidalgo, Blue Mountain, and Sumatra.
varieties.origin: Yemen, via India and Java to Amsterdam; spread across the Americas from 1719
varieties.catalog_summary: One of the most culturally and genetically important C. arabica coffees in the world, with high quality in Central America. Very high susceptibility to coffee leaf rust, well-adapted to the coldest conditions.
varieties.notes: Historically the benchmark cup — clean, sweet, delicate — and still the basis of Jamaican, Peruvian and Dominican coffees. Large beans and very good high-altitude quality, but low yield and extreme rust susceptibility mean small, expensive lots.

varieties.name: Venecia
varieties.breeder: Instituto del Café de Costa Rica (ICAFE)
varieties.catalog_summary: Very high susceptibility to coffee leaf rust. Well-adapted to rainy zones due to late harvest during dry season.
varieties.notes: Very high susceptibility to coffee leaf rust. Well-adapted to rainy zones due to late harvest during dry season. WCR rates high-altitude cup quality potential as good; bean size large; best at medium-to-high elevation for its latitude.

varieties.name: Villa Sarchi
varieties.breeder: Instituto del Café de Costa Rica (ICAFE)
varieties.catalog_summary: Well-adpated to highest altitude conditions and tolerant of strong winds.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Well-adpated to highest altitude conditions and tolerant of strong winds.
varieties.notes: Costa Rican dwarf Bourbon mutation adapted to the highest altitudes and windy sites; one of the two parents (with Caturra) of every Sarchimor. Very good high-altitude cup.

varieties.name: BP 534
varieties.lineage: Individual selection labeled 6 from a Congolensis population.
varieties.breeder: Indonesian Coffee and Cocoa Research Institute (ICCRI)
varieties.catalog_summary: Most commonly grown clone by farmers in Indonesia; suitable for cultivation under agroforestry systems.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Suitable for wet climates in areas with elevation 400–900 meters above sea level. The plant has short internodes. There is a clear white line on green cherry. This clone is susceptible to Pratylenchus coffeae. Must be planted together with other clones to enable fruit set.
varieties.notes: Most commonly grown clone by farmers in Indonesia; suitable for cultivation under agroforestry systems. Bean size large (screen size >17); yield potential 1700-2200 kg/ha; average mucilage content in the cherry.

varieties.name: BP 936
varieties.breeder: Indonesian Coffee and Cocoa Research Institute (ICCRI)
varieties.catalog_summary: Wide adaptability to different environments, with optimal productivity in areas with wet climates; suitable for cultivation under agroforestry systems.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: The clone has wide adaptability, but optimal productivity will be achieved in wet climates areas with elevations ranging from 400–900 meters above sea level. This clone is susceptible to Pratylenchus coffeae. Must be planted together with other clones to enable fruit set.
varieties.notes: Wide adaptability to different environments, with optimal productivity in areas with wet climates; suitable for cultivation under agroforestry systems. Bean size large (screen size >17); yield potential 1600-2200 kg/ha; average mucilage content in the cherry.

varieties.name: BP 939
varieties.breeder: Indonesian Coffee and Cocoa Research Institute (ICCRI)
varieties.catalog_summary: Wide adaptability to different environments that produces best in areas with dry climates; suitable for cultivation under agroforestry systems.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: The clone has wide adaptability but optimal productivity will be achieved in dry climate areas with altitudes ranging between 400–900 meters above sea level. This clone is susceptible to Pratylenchus coffeae. Must be planted together with other clones to enable fruit set.
varieties.notes: Wide adaptability to different environments that produces best in areas with dry climates; suitable for cultivation under agroforestry systems. Bean size large (screen size >17); yield potential 1400-1900 kg/ha; average mucilage content in the cherry.

varieties.name: BRS 1216
varieties.catalog_summary: Adaptable to the environments of the Western Amazon with high productivity. Plant structure suitable for mechanized harvesting. Resistant to nematodes and coffee rust.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: High yield per hectare when established in full sun with no shade. When in an environment with low water availability in the soil, it shows generalized yellowing. Overall beverage quality score (Specialty Coffee Association) = 79 points. Flavor attributes: Chocolate, cereals, woody. Highest fruit set will occur when planted with other clones in gametophytic compatibility Groups II and III, as this variety is from Group I.
varieties.notes: Adaptable to the environments of the Western Amazon with high productivity. Plant structure suitable for mechanized harvesting. Resistant to nematodes and coffee rust. Bean size medium (screen size 15-16); yield potential 7200 kg/ha; high mucilage content in the cherry.

varieties.name: BRS 2299
varieties.lineage: Unknown parents. Natural cross between conilon and robusta plants. These were selected from farmers' fields.
varieties.catalog_summary: Plant structure suitable for mechanized harvesting. Stands out for its tolerance to the root-knot nematode Meloidogyne sp.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Presents high yield per hectare when established in full sun with no shade. It can present a greater unevenness in the ripening of fruits, caused by irregular flowering in years of greater rain frequency during the dry season. Overall beverage quality score (Specialty Coffee Association) = 70 points. Flavor attributes: Neutral, cereal, herbal. Highest fruit set will occur when planted with other clones in gametophytic compatibility Groups I and III, as this variety is from Group II.
varieties.notes: Plant structure suitable for mechanized harvesting. Stands out for its tolerance to the root-knot nematode Meloidogyne sp. Bean size medium (screen size 15-16); yield potential 6600 kg/ha; average mucilage content in the cherry.

varieties.name: BRS 2314
varieties.catalog_summary: High cupping scores; has been classified as a 'fine robusta.'
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Presents high yield per hectare under irrigation. This cultivar has received 80 points or more in all the cupping events conducted, reaching 87.2 points in one of the samples. Following the Fine Robustas Tasting Protocol developed by the Coffee Quality Institute, it has been classified as a 'Fine Robusta.' Average beverage quality score (Specialty Coffee Association) = 80 points. Flavor attributes: chocolate, caramel, fruit. Highest fruit set will occur when planted with other clones in gametophytic compatibility Groups I and III, as this variety is from Group II.
varieties.notes: High cupping scores; has been classified as a 'fine robusta.'. Bean size small (screen size 14 or below); yield potential 6600 kg/ha; average mucilage content in the cherry.

varieties.name: BRS 2336
varieties.lineage: Unknown parents. Natural cross between conilon and robusta plants. These were selected from farmers' fields.
varieties.catalog_summary: Adaptable to the environments of the Western Amazon, with high productivity and bean size.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Presents high yield per hectare when established in full sun with no shade. Resistant to water stress; however, irrigation is recommended. Leaves demonstrate the behavior of plants under water stress, even in conditions of high water availability. Beverage quality score (Specialty Coffee Association) = 75 points. Flavor attributes: sweet aftertaste, soft. Highest fruit set will occur when planted with other clones in gametophytic compatibility Groups I and III, as this variety is from Group II.
varieties.notes: Adaptable to the environments of the Western Amazon, with high productivity and bean size. Bean size medium (screen size 15-16); yield potential 7200 kg/ha; high mucilage content in the cherry.

varieties.name: BRS 2357
varieties.lineage: Unknown parents. Natural cross between conilon and robusta plants. These were selected from farmers' fields.
varieties.catalog_summary: Compact canopy, which allows for densification. Short stems allow one additional harvest before renewal.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Presents high yield per hectare when established in full sun with no shade. It has small, narrow leaves that allow good air circulation inside its crown. It is susceptible to the root-knot nematode, and is susceptible to coffee leaf rust. Beverage quality score (Specialty Coffee Association) = 70 points. Flavor attributes: neutral, no attributes worth highlighting. Highest fruit set will occur when planted with other clones in gametophytic compatibility Groups I and III, as this variety is from Group II.
varieties.notes: Compact canopy, which allows for densification. Short stems allow one additional harvest before renewal. Bean size medium (screen size 15-16); yield potential 6000 kg/ha; average mucilage content in the cherry.

varieties.name: BRS 3137
varieties.lineage: Unknown parents. Natural cross between conilon and robusta plants. These were selected from farmers' fields.
varieties.catalog_summary: Recognized for its rusticity, presenting good vegetative and productive characteristics in dry conditions and low-fertility soils.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Beverage quality score (Speciality Coffee Association) = 70 points. Flavor attributes: neutral. Highest fruit set will occur when planted with other clones in gametophytic compatibility Groups I and II, as this variety is from Group III.
varieties.notes: Recognized for its rusticity, presenting good vegetative and productive characteristics in dry conditions and low-fertility soils. Bean size small (screen size 14 or below); yield potential 6600 kg/ha; average mucilage content in the cherry.

varieties.name: BRS 3193
varieties.lineage: Unknown parents. Natural cross between conilon and robusta plants. These were selected from farmers' fields.
varieties.catalog_summary: Long primary branches. Production peak in the second or third commercial harvest due to its initial growth, which reduces the biannual production of the crop by compensating for lower yields of other clones.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Recognized for having the longest length of productive branches among the genotypes studied, and for presenting with a high number of rosettes per branch. Beverage quality score (Specialty Coffee Association) = 75 points. Flavor attributes: chocolate, caramel, almond. Highest fruit set will occur when planted with other clones in gametophytic compatibility Groups I and II, as this variety is from Group III.
varieties.notes: Long primary branches. Production peak in the second or third commercial harvest due to its initial growth, which reduces the biannual production of the crop by compensating for lower yields of other clones. Bean size small (screen size 14 or below); yield potential 6000 kg/ha; average mucilage content in the cherry.

varieties.name: BRS 3210
varieties.lineage: Unknown parents. Natural cross between conilon and robusta plants. These were selected from farmers' fields.
varieties.catalog_summary: Good adaptability and stability in the environments of the Western Amazon. Good productivity and bean size.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Resistant to water stress, however, irrigation is recommended. Even in conditions of high water availability, its leaves demonstrate the behavior of plants under water stress. Presents high yield per hectare, 120 60-kg bags. Beverage quality score (Specialty Coffee Association) = 75 points. Attributes: Sweet aftertaste, soft. This cultivar is established in full sun with no shade. Highest fruit set will occur when planted with other clones in gametophytic compatibility Groups I and II, as this variety is from Group III.
varieties.notes: Good adaptability and stability in the environments of the Western Amazon. Good productivity and bean size. Bean size medium (screen size 15-16); yield potential 7200 kg/ha; high mucilage content in the cherry.

varieties.name: BRS 3213
varieties.lineage: Unknown parents. Natural cross between conilon and robusta plants. These were selected from farmers' fields.
varieties.catalog_summary: Adaptable to the environments of the Western Amazon recognized for good productivity and bean size.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Presents high yield per hectare when established in full sun with no shade. Resistant to water stress, however, irrigation is recommended. Even in conditions of high water availability, its leaves demonstrate the behavior of plants under water stress. Beverage quality score (Specialty Coffee Association) = 75 points. Flavor atributes: sweet aftertaste, soft. Highest fruit set will occur when planted with other clones in gametophytic compatibility Groups I and II, as this variety is from Group III.
varieties.notes: Adaptable to the environments of the Western Amazon recognized for good productivity and bean size. Bean size medium (screen size 15-16); yield potential 7200 kg/ha; high mucilage content in the cherry.

varieties.name: BRS 3220
varieties.lineage: Unknown parents. Natural cross between conilon and robusta plants. These were selected from farmers' fields.
varieties.catalog_summary: Adaptable to the environments of the Western Amazon, recognized for good productivity and bean size.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Presents high yield per hectare when established in full sun with no shade. Resistant to water stress, however, irrigation is recommended. Even in conditions of high water availability, its leaves demonstrate the behavior of plants under water stress. Beverage quality score (Specialty Coffee Association) = 75 points. Flavor attributes: sweet aftertaste, soft. Highest fruit set will occur when planted with other clones in gametophytic compatibility Groups I and II, as this variety is from Group III.
varieties.notes: Adaptable to the environments of the Western Amazon, recognized for good productivity and bean size. Bean size medium (screen size 15-16); yield potential 6600 kg/ha; high mucilage content in the cherry.

varieties.name: INIFAP 00-24
varieties.breeder: Nestlé Research/Instituto Nacional de Investigaciones Forestales Agricolas y Pecuarias
varieties.catalog_summary: Compact plant grown under the conditions of the Chiapas coast in Mexico. Reduced plant size lends itself to higher yields in dry conditions and differentiates it from any other clone.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Has the tendency to produce more than three productive stems per plant with heavy fruit load. Combined with typical multiplication by rooted cuttings, it means the plant may need to be staked. However, this typically does not become a problem and rather facilitates the harvest. Usually cultivated at 700 meters above sea level. Must be planted together with other clones to enable fruit set.
varieties.notes: Compact plant grown under the conditions of the Chiapas coast in Mexico. Reduced plant size lends itself to higher yields in dry conditions and differentiates it from any other clone. Bean size medium (screen size 15-16); low mucilage content in the cherry.

varieties.name: INIFAP 00-28
varieties.breeder: Nestlé Research/Instituto Nacional de Investigaciones Forestales Agricolas y Pecuarias (INIFAP)
varieties.catalog_summary: Tall plants with large and numerous leaves and fruits; highest-yielding clone for the conditions of the coast of Chiapas, Mexico.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: This clone does not produce many shoots and, normally, the plant is formed with 1 or 2 productive stems. Susceptible to stem and shoot hole borer and coffee berry disease (CBD). Typically cultivated at 700 meters above sea level. Must be planted together with other clones to enable fruit set.
varieties.notes: Tall plants with large and numerous leaves and fruits; highest-yielding clone for the conditions of the coast of Chiapas, Mexico. Bean size medium (screen size 15-16); low mucilage content in the cherry.

varieties.name: INIFAP 95-9
varieties.catalog_summary: Tall plant with very large fruit. Susceptible to shoot hole borer.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: This clone is preferred by growers in the coastal region of Chiapas, Mexico. Farmers coloquially refer to it as 'improved robusta' due to its fruit size, which is reflected in good production per unit area. It is susceptible to coffee berry borer; no rust damage has been observed. The multiplication is via seed, which does not guarantee homogeneity of the resulting population. Mucilage detaches easily through pulping and fermentation. This clone is typically cultivated at 700 meters above sea level. Must be planted together with other clones to enable fruit set.
varieties.notes: Tall plant with very large fruit. Susceptible to shoot hole borer. Bean size large (screen size >17); average mucilage content in the cherry.

varieties.name: INIFAP 97-14
varieties.catalog_summary: Tall growth, tendency to form plants with more than three productive stems and good yield of cherries. Very susceptible to stem borers and anthracnose.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Alternates high and low production years. Susceptible to stem and shoot hole borer and leaf anthracnose. The weight of its production can overwhelm the stems. Typically cultivated at 700 meters above sea level. Must be planted together with other clones to enable fruit set.
varieties.notes: Tall growth, tendency to form plants with more than three productive stems and good yield of cherries. Very susceptible to stem borers and anthracnose. Bean size medium (screen size 15-16); low mucilage content in the cherry.

varieties.name: INIFAP 97-15
varieties.catalog_summary: Tall growth, tendency to form plants with more than three productive stems. Good yield potential, wide range of adaptation to the climatic conditions of the coast of Chiapas and Veracruz, Mexico.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Susceptible to coffee leaf rust, anthracnose, and coffee thread blight. However, it offers a good range of adaptation to different environments. varieties.notes: Tall growth, tendency to form plants with more than three productive stems. Good yield potential, wide range of adaptation to the climatic conditions of the coast of Chiapas and Veracruz, Mexico. Bean size medium (screen size 15-16); low mucilage content in the cherry.

varieties.notes: Suitable for cultivation under agroforestry systems in areas with dry climates. Bean size large (screen size >17); yield potential 800-2100 kg/ha; average mucilage content in the cherry.

varieties.name: Sln.1R
varieties.lineage: Coffea congensis x Coffea canephora and recurrent back cross to Robusta. Selection from BC2.
varieties.breeder: Central Coffee Research Institute (CCRI), Coffee Board of India
varieties.catalog_summary: Plants that are very vigorous and grow into moderately large trees.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: This variety is composed of two clones—S.270 and S.274—which are required to be planted together, because separate planting will reduce fruit sets.These two genotypes have recorded yields of nearly 1000 kg/ha on an average over 35 years of testing in rain-fed conditions. The planting density for this variety is 3m x 3m.
varieties.notes: Plants that are very vigorous and grow into moderately large trees. Bean size medium (screen size 15-16); yield potential 1500-3000 kg/ha.

varieties.name: Sln.2R
varieties.breeder: Central Coffee Research Institute (CCRI), Coffee Board of India
varieties.catalog_summary: Plants that are very vigorous and grow into moderately large trees and produce large beans.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Many agronomic traits of Sln.2R, including yield potential, resemble Sln.1R. However, these clones have a higher stability for A-grade beans than the Sln.1R. This variety is composed of a mixture of three clones—BR 9, 10, and 11—which are required to be planted in mixtures, because separate planting will reduce fruit sets. Yield of up to 1,500 kg/ha in wet and shaded conditions and up to 2,500 kg/ha when managed carefully, including supplementary irrigation and flowering management.
varieties.notes: Plants that are very vigorous and grow into moderately large trees and produce large beans. Bean size large (screen size >17); yield potential 1500-3000 kg/ha.

varieties.catalog_summary: Compact plant stature with good yielding potential, suitable for high-density planting.
varieties.additional_agronomic_information: Relatively high water requirement for blossom and backing compared to other Robusta varieties. It is considered year-1 producing when using clones. If using seed, it will produce in year 2 and year 3, when cultivated under shade. Using irrigation can assist with early ripening. The planting density for this variety ranges from to 2.4m x 2.4m to 2.7m x 2.7m. Cultivated at altitudes of 500 to 1000 meters above sea level. Yield of up to 1500 kg/ha under rain-fed and shaded conditions and up to 2500 kg/ha under intensive cultivation practices including blossom & backing irrigation.
varieties.notes: Compact plant stature with good yielding potential, suitable for high-density planting. Bean size large (screen size >17); yield potential 1500-2500 kg/ha; high mucilage content in the cherry.
